question: A 23-year-old man presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath. The patient was at a lunch hosted by his employer. He started to feel his symptoms begin when he started playing football outside with a few of the other employees. The patient has a past medical history of atopic dermatitis and asthma. His temperature is 98.3°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 87/58 mmHg, pulse is 150/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 85% on room air. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
enhanced_information: The patient presenting with shortness of breath, tachycardia, hypotension, and hypoxemia likely has an acute severe asthma exacerbation. The best next step in management is to administer albuterol and prednisone to address bronchoconstriction and inflammation.
analysis: The patient's presentation with shortness of breath, tachycardia, hypotension, and hypoxemia suggests an acute severe asthma exacerbation. The best next step in management aligns with standard medical knowledge, which involves administering albuterol and prednisone to address bronchoconstriction and inflammation in asthma exacerbations.
